Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry experiment specifically aimed to identify ESCO2-interacting proteins in response to DNA damage, using bleomycin as the inducing agent and comparing the results against a negative control group.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: The experiment is an affinity purification (IP-MS) using Flag-tagged ESCO2. While PRIDE metadata mentions 'Spectrum count/molecular weight', the overall design is a label-free comparison between a bait group and a negative control group.

workflow: HEK293T cells were lysed in modified RIPA buffer, sonicated, and precleared with protein G beads. The supernatants were incubated with anti-Flag affinity beads at 4°C for 4 h and eluted with Flag peptide.
The MS data were aligned with the Human Reviewed Swiss-Prot database by Proteome Discoverer 2.2 software.

Proteins were considered to be major hits (positive) when matching the following criteria: (i) not found in negative control group; (ii) high Protein FDR Confidence (FDR < 0.01) and (iii) peptides >= 5.
differential: Proteins were considered to be major hits (positive) when matching the following criteria: (i) not found in negative control group

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: The proteomics part of this study is a straightforward AP-MS to identify ESCO2 interactors. Although the broader paper discusses phosphorylation (S196, T233) and acetylation (SMC3 K105/106), the PRIDE metadata explicitly states 'No PTMs are included in the dataset' for the MS analysis, and the methods describe a protein-level identification filter.
